rules.statement: When the same API operations serve several kinds of owner, expose one endpoint and one hook per operation that takes a discriminated-union owner parameter. Do not write a copy per owner kind, and do not use a factory that generates a named set per kind.
rules.why: With per-owner copies, a fix lands in one copy and misses the others. Hook names produced by a factory can't be found by searching for them.
rules.check: Look for new endpoints, hooks or UI tabs that repeat an existing operation for one owner kind (for example useListTenantSecretsQuery next to useListClientSecretsQuery), or factories that build endpoint names per kind.

rules.statement: Build an owner's API path with the single shared helper that applies the scope prefix rules and URI-encodes every id. Callers must not concatenate paths themselves.
rules.why: Paths built by hand repeat the scope-prefix and encoding rules, and they drift or skip encoding.
rules.check: Look for template-string or concatenated API paths in endpoints or callers that insert ids directly instead of calling the shared owner-path helper, especially ids without encodeURIComponent.

rules.statement: URI-encode every id embedded in a composite cache-tag key, so that delimiter characters such as ':' in an id can't produce a key that equals another entity's tag.
rules.why: Without encoding, the key for an id like 'x:effective' could equal the effective-settings tag of id 'x', and invalidating one owner's cache would also invalidate another's.
rules.check: Look for cache tag ids or keys built by joining raw ids with ':' or another separator, without encoding.

rules.statement: Cache tags must be scoped to both the owner and the scope it is administered in. A mutation must invalidate only its own owner's tags, so it never refetches another owner's data in the same scope or a different one.
rules.why: Keeping each scope's cached data apart is what stops one owner's or scope's caches from invalidating another's.
rules.check: Check that providesTags and invalidatesTags use owner- and scope-qualified ids, not a bare tag type, an unscoped id, or a broad tag that covers other owners.

rules.statement: When an operation is valid for only one member of an owner union, type its parameter as that narrowed member, so the type checker rejects calls for other owner kinds. Have the UI offer the operation only for that kind.
rules.why: The backend supports the operation, secret rotation, for that kind alone, so the restriction is enforced through types rather than at runtime.
rules.check: Look for a single-kind operation whose parameter is typed as the whole owner union, or UI that offers it for every owner kind.
